Heuer timers sold by dealers in Swimming World from February 1960. Seagull ads May 1977 to October 1978: LCD
Microsplit, 59:59.99 range, 1/100 s, said to draw a twelfth of what an LED watch does; a slogan that a quarter of all stopwatches sold were Heuers; Heuer 230 Microsplit, $69.95, one battery every two years (September 1978). Seagull
wrote from a Timing Products Division by August 1978. Swim News n46 lists Heuer among the companies Seagull
said made up Swiss Timing at that date. Ads under Heuer's own name continue (December 1981).

Company history, the later TAG Heuer name and the Swiss Timing link were not researched.

This article is a stub. Heuer is a Swiss stopwatch maker whose LCD Microsplit stopwatches
[Seagull Enterprises](seagull.md) sold in the United States from 1977.

See the [vendors](index.md) register for the companies this wiki covers.
